name: Doorbell
tagline: Biometric desktop lockbox with motorized latch and security chime
summary: Hasp is a programmable smart desktop vault with a motorized deadbolt driven by an SG90 micro-servo. An interactive authentication trigger simulates biometric verification, updating the OLED display, sounding confirmation chimes, and actuating the reinforced latch mechanism.

parts.name: Arduino Uno R3
parts.why: Controller executing authentication verification, servo PWM deadbolt control, and security timers.

parts.name: TowerPro SG90 9g Micro Servo Motor
parts.why: High-torque nylon gear micro servo driving physical 90-degree vault latch mechanism.

parts.name: 5V Active Piezo Buzzer
parts.why: Emits distinct authentication feedback chimes and tamper warning tones.

parts.name: 0.96 inch I2C OLED Display
parts.why: Visual interface displaying lock state, authorization status, and countdown timer.

parts.name: 18650 Li-ion Battery Holder with DC Jack
parts.why: Provides high peak current required during servo latch engagement.

tests.name: Lockbox Retains Locked State Under Idle

product.pageHeadline: Motorized personal desktop security made tangible.
bullets: Rugged SG-90 micro servo deadbolt with 90-degree positive physical latching
Dual visual and acoustic validation indicators with live countdown timers
Reinforced 2.5mm thick walls with concealed internal hinge geometry
Low standby quiescent draw with battery-backup support for 18650 cells

buildSteps: Step 1: 3D print the Hasp reinforced security body and top lid with 2.5mm walls.
Step 2: Screw the SG90 micro-servo into the internal latch bracket.
Step 3: Attach the locking latch arm to the servo horn and calibrate 0-90 degree travel.
Step 4: Mount the Arduino Uno and wire the D9 PWM control line to the servo.
Step 5: Wire the OLED display to A4/A5 and install the piezo buzzer on D8.
Step 6: Power on, trigger biometric simulated authentication, and verify deadbolt actuation.
